work: Hieronymus Bosch, The Garden of Earthly Delights triptych
current_project_images: Two AI-assisted reinterpretations inspired by Bosch. The aligned garden and aftermath layouts are this project's invention, not two original paintings or a historically literal reconstruction.
theological_distinction: The original right panel depicts Hell, not Purgatory. In Catholic teaching Purgatory is a final purification of those assured salvation, distinct from the punishment of the damned. Seasonal recovery in our Aftermath is a contemporary artistic extension, not a literal account of Catholic Hell.

panels.subject: Paradise / Eden: God presents Eve to Adam.
panels.context: Genesis and the institution of marriage; distinguish this panel from the central garden.

panels.subject: Earthly pleasures: nude figures, oversized fruit, animals and fantastic constructions.
panels.interpretation: The Prado catalogue reads it as a deceptive paradise of lust. Sweet fruit and fragile enclosures can make fleeting pleasure visible. This does not settle every disputed motif.

panels.subject: Hell: ruined and burning landscapes, punishment, creatures and oversized musical instruments.
panels.interpretation: Moral consequences and reversal of pleasure into pain; also social satire. This is not a literal illustration of a single Bible passage.

panels.subject: Creation of the world, traditionally the third day; Creator and Latin inscriptions.
panels.context: Creation imagery related to Genesis; catalogue identifies inscriptions with Psalms 33:9 and 148:5.

research_based_design_connection.author: Margaret D. Carroll
research_based_design_connection.source: Time and Transformation: Hieronymus Bosch’s Process, Yale University Press, 2022
research_based_design_connection.claim_status: An attributed scholarly interpretation, not proven authorial intent or universal consensus.
research_based_design_connection.reading: The work can be read through world history, generation and decline, transient light, water and flame, and motifs transformed between panels.
research_based_design_connection.project_inference: Environmental time and transformation can provide a stronger narrative basis than adding decorative motion. Endless growth versus the need for rest is our contemporary interpretive extension, not Bosch's documented environmental message.
